protocol:
Tiny Earth Gram Stain Test Protocol 
  
 Gram stains of Ab+isolates were done by collecting a sample of its bacterial colony and smearing the sample into a drop of sterile water on a microscope slide. After leaving the smear to completely air dry, slides were heat fixed, flooded with crystal violet dye for 1 minute, gently rinsed with sterile water and gently patted between bibulous paper to produce a primary stain. The smear was then flooded with the mordant Gram iodine for 1 minute and once again rinsed and blotted. To decolorize, holding the slide at a 45 angle, a continuous stream of ethanol was used to flood the slide for 5-10 seconds and then immediately rinsed. As a counterstain, the slide was flooded with safranin for 1 minute, rinsed and blotted. Slides were then viewed under a microscope with oil immersion for greater visualization.

Gram Staining Of Fixed Bacterial 
 Samples 
 Note: All staining is done in the laboratory sink and we do not let the stain flow 
 down the drain. Please collect the waste in plastic container found in the sink. 
 Once the plastic container is full, please let the instructor know and they can 
 direct you to how to dispose of the waste. 
  
 Primary stain 
  
 1. Use the bottle-top dropper to flood the heat-fixed smears with crystal violet dye 
 2. Stain for 1 minute 
 3. Use a gentle, steady stream of tap water from the faucet at your sink to rinse 
 off excess crystal violet dye until the water flowing off the slide is colorless 
 a. Use a clothespin to hold slide 1 on the left, short edge at a 45º angle 
 b. Carefully hold the slide under a trickle of tap water 
 c. Return slide to the slide rack 
  
 Mordant 
  
 1. Use the bottle-top dropper to flood slides with iodine completely covering all fixed, 
 stained bacterial samples. 
 2. Allow the mordant to bind to crystal violet for 1 minute 
 3. Use the clothespin to hold and rinse each slide with tap water as described 
 above. 
  
 Decolorization 
  
 1. Use the clothespin to hold slides at a 45 angle and flood with ethanol by applying 
 a continuous stream for 5 seconds. 
 2. Take caution not to over or under-decolorize the samples. 
 3. Rinse immediately with tap water as described above. 
 4. Return slides to the slide rack. 
 Counterstain 
 1. Use bottle-top dropper to flood the slide with safranin 
 2. Counterstain for 1 minute 
 3. Use the clothespin to hold and rinse each slide with tap water as described 
 above. 
 Prior to visualization, lightly pat each slide with either bibulous paper or a paper towel 
  
 View at 40X

protocol:
Supplies needed: 
 Streak plate or stock plate (more recent works best) 
 Known Gram + and Gram - control bacteria 
 Sterile toothpicks 
 Clean microscope slide 
 Paper towel 
 Microscope and immersion oil 
 Ethanol lamp 
 Gram stain set  
  
 Protocol: 
 1. Draw a circle on a clean, dry microscope slide and label with a sample ID near the edge. 
 2. Pipet 2 ul of sterile water in the center of the circle you drew. 
 3. Collect a small sample of a bacterial colony with the tip of a toothpick. 
 4. Make a smear of the sample within the circle you drew on the slide. Let it dry. 
 5. Fix cells by passing the slide through the flame of the ethanol lamp 3 or 4 times, with the smear facing up. Be careful to not burn yourself on the flame or with the hot glass slide. 
 6. For the staining steps, you will need to work by a sink or over a tray/tub to discard the excess stain and rinses. 
 7. Flood the smear with crystal violet and let it sit for 1 minute. 
 8. Gently rinse the slide with an indirect stream of water from a squirt bottle for about 2 seconds. Blot the edge of the slide on a paper towel. Do not wipe the smear.  
 9. Flood the smear with Gram iodine. Wait for 1 minute. 
 10. Gently rinse with water as before and blot the edge of the slide on a paper towel. 
 11. Drip 95% ethanol across the smear until the solution runs clear (less than 15 seconds). 
 12. Briefly rinse with water and blot the edge of the slide with a paper towel. 
 13. Flood the smear with safranin for 1 minute. 
 14. Gently rinse with water and blot the edge of the slide with a paper towel. 
 15. Let the slide air dry for several minutes. Excess liquid can be blotted off the underside of the slide but do not wipe the smear. 
 16. View slide under the microscope starting at low power and progressing to 100X with oil immersion.   
 17. Take an image of focused cells using the SPOT Basic software and include the images in your lab notebook. There should be one microscope with a camera at each bench. Spot Basic Software instructions below.

 Each group has one microscope with a camera attached that connects to a biology department laptop via USB cable. These cameras work with software called SPOT Basic on the laptops. The following instructions will walk you through how to adjust settings and save images using the software. 
  
 Once you have a specimen in focus on the microscope, you are ready to test out the imaging software. Make sure the camera is attached to the laptop computer by a USB cable and is getting power (green light on camera should be illuminated). 
  Open the SPOT Basic software on the toolbar.

You may need to adjust the focus of the camera to match the focus of the microscope. To do this rotate the black tube (HR Coupler) that attaches the camera to the scope until the Live Image is also in focus.

 If your image seems too bright or too dim, you can adjust the light intensity and contrast on your microscope to correct. Or you can click on the Image Settings button and make adjustments.

You can delete, move or make changes as needed. To make sure that your calibration mark saves with your image, go to Edit > Merge Objects > Merge Calibration Marks. This will save the scale bar with your image file.

protocol:
Procedure  
  
 Label two slides with initials, period and culture number in small writing at edge of slide.   
  
 Fill water cups with tap water for dunking slides  
  
 Take your inoculating loop and dunk loop in water. Spread film of water in loop on the center of one slide. Repeat with other slide. Remember, the more water you have, the more time to dry so don’t over do it.   
  
 Using a toothpick, add a small amount of bacterial culture to corresponding slides, mixing well in the water you added. Use a separate toothpick for your second slide. Remember, less is more here.   
  
 Use the toothpick to spread out the water/bacteria mix to make a film across the center of the slide.    
  
 Allow slides to completely air dry.   
  
 Light burner.   
  
 Using clothespin, hold your slide on one side and pass through the flame 3 times, 1 second each pass. Repeat for other 2 slides.   
  
 Add enough crystal violet to cover your bacterial. Wait 60 seconds.  
  
 Dip slides into beaker of water to rinse. Tap edge of each slide on paper towel to remove excess water.   
  
 Add 4 drops of iodine to each fixed area of bacteria. Wait 60 seconds.   
  
 Dip slides into beaker of water to rinse. Tap edge of each slide on paper towel to remove excess water.   
  
 Hold each slide over your beaker at an angle and using your plastic pipette, pipette ethanol down the slide, rinsing off the stain. Only use enough ethanol to remove the stain.   
  
 Add 4 drops of Safranin to the fixed bacterial area on your slide. Wait 60 seconds.   
  
 Dip slides into beaker of water to rinse. Tap edge of each slide on paper towel to remove excess water.   
  
 Dry the slide by blotting (not rubbing!) a paper towel on each slide.   
  
 You are ready for the microscope on day 2. Place slides in white holding container until the next day.
